question.text: The first Persian invasion of Greece was led by this Persian ruler in order to punish them for their participation in the Ionian Revolt. This man divided his empire into satraps.
question.clue: The Ionian Revolt prompted this man to plan an invasion of the Greek mainland which ended with a loss at Marathon.

swap.leadin: A military operation in this country called Operation Eagle Claw was authorized only when Secretary of State Cyrus Vance took a brief vacation and was not present to oppose the plan.
swap.text: Name this country that took 52 Americans hostage in 1979 and released them moments after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as President in 1981.
swap.clue: This country has the 2nd largest gas reserves in the world, and is the 4th largest producer of petroleum.

question.text: Leonidas' 300 Spartans were defeated by this empire's much larger force: over 2 million troops if you believe Herodotus, which scholars don't. Xerxes [zerk-zees] led this empire against the Greeks, but was defeated at the naval Battle of Salamis.
question.clue: A ruler of this empire was assassinated by Artabanus, the commander of this empire's royal bodyguard, the Immortals.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the role of the pythia in Ancient Greece.
swap.text: The second Persian invasion of Greece was led by this monarch, the son of Darius I. While victorious at Thermopylae, his armies were defeated at Platea after they burned Athens.
swap.clue: In an inscription from his reign, he claims to have destroyed the den of the daivas, leading some to believe that this man was religiously intolerant.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
question.text: At the Battle of Dara, Belisarius defeated forces under this empire, who were known for their heavy armored horsemen called cataphracts. Later, the Byzantine Empire established the Eternal Peace with its leader Khosrau I (KHOO-shuh-roo "the first").
question.clue: One king of this dynasty was crowned in utero, while another may have either flayed the skin of a noted captive or poured molten gold down his throat after forcing him and his army to work on an aqueduct, the Band-e-Kaisar.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about civilizations that relied on horse archers.
swap.text: Retreating horse archers would turn around to shoot arrows at the enemy in a "shot" named for this empire. This Persian empire between that of the Seleucids and the Sassanids used horse archers in their defeat of Crassus at the Battle of Carrhae.
swap.answerHtml: Parthian Empire [accept Arsacid dynasty or empire; accept Parthian shot]
swap.clue: At one battle, a general of this empire ordered his soldiers to cover their horses with cloth, thereby disguising the gleam of their armor.

question.text: This Elamite city served as the capital of Cyrus the Great before Xerxes' father Darius I built a new one at Persepolis.
question.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

swap.leadin: This man named 16 cities after his father, Antiochus.
swap.text: Name this general who served under a famous Macedonian king during his Asian campaigns. He was also the first ruler of a namesake empire, the easternmost of the Macedonian successor states.
swap.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

question.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
question.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

swap.text: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.
swap.clue: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the generals who carved up Alexander the Great's empire after his death, the Diadochi.
question.text: This man managed to grab the lion's share of the empire, taking Mesopotamia, Persia, and Bactria. He later fought an unsuccessful war with Chandragupta Maurya.
question.clue: This ruler, one of Alexander the Great's successors, who established a namesake Hellenistic kingdom in western Asia and was succeeded by his son Antiochus I.

swap.leadin: A ruler of this empire became the youngest king ever when a crown was placed on his mother's belly, thus crowning him before he was even born.
swap.text: Name this powerful Persian empire which lasted from the 3rd century to the 7th century. In its conflicts with Rome, this empire's ruler Shapur II captured Roman emperor Valerian and turned him into a footstool.
swap.answerHtml: Sassanid Empire [or the Sassanian Empire; prompt on Persia]
swap.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

question.text: Many Neo-Hittite states to the south spoke this Semitic language that replaced Akkadian to become the lingua franca of the Near East
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.text: The Behistun inscription is written in Old Persian, Babylonian, and the language of these peoples, whose capital was Susa. This civilization's Old dynasties included the Awan, Simashki, and Epartid.
swap.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

question.text: The Parthian ruling dynasty was named after this founding ruler, who ruled from the city of Nisa after he conquered a satrapy from the anti-Seleucid rebel Andragoras.

swap.leadin: This city fell soon after the Battle of al-Qadisayyah.
swap.text: Name this city across the river from Seleucia-on-the-Tigris, which served as the capital of both the Parthian and Sassanian Empires.
swap.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

question.text: An "archaeological complex" named for Bactria and this region was home to Gonur Depe ("go-NOOR deh-PEH"), where Harappan seals have been found. A much later mention of this region's name appears in the Behistun Inscription, which records the rebellion of Frada there.
question.answerHtml: Margiana [or Marguš or Margush or Margiane or Marv; accept Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex; accept Frāda of Margiana]

swap.leadin: George Rawlinson re-read Strabo's claim that these people required that men must have at least five wives as a misinterpretation of a limit on the size of their harems.
swap.text: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg quipped that what people's short-lived empire "exists for us because Herodotus said it did," referencing the historian's questionable accounts of kings like Deioces and Astyages?
swap.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a delightful tale of deception, cannibalism, and betrayal.
question.text: This general had to eat his own son after Astyages discovered he did not actually murder an infant prophesied to overthrow him. He would later understandably mutiny against Astyages at the Battle of Pasargadae.
question.clue: Upon arriving in Susa, Alexander found that this treasurer had taken large quantities of money and soldiers and bolted town for Athens. This man was eventually killed in Crete.

swap.leadin: Name these people or battles important in Cyrus' establishment of the Persian Empire, FTP each.
swap.text: Cyrus began his conquest by overthrowing this Median king, the son of Cyaxares, and, according to Herodotus, Cyrus' grandfather.
swap.clue: The son of Cyaxares and grandfather of Cyrus the Great, he ruled as the last king of the Medes until Cyrus overthrew him.
